stories.title: Helsing unveils Clarity, an AI system that preps targets for weapons systems
stories.summary: Defense company Helsing launched Clarity, an AI platform that fuses sensor data into target recommendations for weapons systems under human oversight, but past incidents raise concerns about automation risks.
stories.more: Clarity is positioned under European control, with every decision said to carry a human name attached for accountability. The report cites experience from the Iran war, Gaza, and a near-miss involving China as reasons that the speed of automated sensor fusion and targeting can create risks that are hard to contain. Human oversight is presented as the main safeguard against those risks. The report doesn't specify what technical limits, if any, constrain how quickly Clarity's recommendations can be acted on.

stories.title: US data brokers reportedly sell $500M in AI training data to Chinese labs
stories.summary: A ChinaTalk investigation reportedly found US data brokers like Mercor, Surge AI, and AfterQuery selling about half a billion dollars' worth of RL training environments to Chinese AI labs, including some originally built for OpenAI or Anthropic.
stories.more: At least nine firms are reportedly involved in these sales. Export controls are said to barely apply to this kind of data, letting US-built training environments reach Chinese labs with little restriction. Some of the environments being sold were originally developed for OpenAI or Anthropic, according to the investigation. The report doesn't specify which Chinese labs are buying the data or what they're using it for.

stories.title: Security firm finds 35,000+ exposed Grok-built apps leaking private data
stories.summary: Security firm Claroc found over 35,000 apps built with Grok exposed to anyone online, including patient data and confidential SpaceXSI documents, caused by a default "anyone with the link" access setting.
stories.more: The root cause identified was that Grok's app-building tool preselected "anyone with the link" as the default sharing setting, leaving apps open without any login. Exposed data reportedly included patient records and plaintext passwords, alongside SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline documents. SpaceXSI took only its own 24 employee-built apps offline after the exposure was found; the rest of the 35,000-plus apps reportedly remain accessible. The report doesn't say whether the default sharing setting itself has since been changed.

stories.title: UK regulator threatens university sanctions over AI-proof exam formats
stories.summary: England's Office for Students says AI has made it "nearly impossible" to fairly assess coursework and is threatening sanctions unless universities adopt AI-proof exam formats, after finding students using ChatGPT to write undetected papers.
stories.more: An investigation cited in the report found students having ChatGPT write entire papers without detection, with some unable to recall basic content from those papers afterward. The regulator frames this as a threat to the credibility of degrees generally. Universities are being told to return to more traditional exam formats or face sanctions. The report doesn't give a compliance deadline or specify what the sanctions would involve.

stories.title: Google launches Tabletop, an AI tool for building group collaboration spaces
stories.summary: Google Labs released Tabletop, an experimental app that lets groups describe what they need and get a custom collaborative hub—itineraries, polls, brackets—generated by AI. It's available via waitlist.
stories.more: Tabletop resembles workplace management apps like Asana and Monday but adds a built-in AI feature that lets users describe what they want and generate a personalized interactive tool from that description. It's aimed at coordinating with family and friends as well as work teams. Users can build things like interactive itineraries, polls, and brackets inside the tool. Access is currently limited to a waitlist, so broader availability details aren't yet known.

stories.title: Adobe previews AI experiments to explore photos in 3D and interview characters
stories.summary: At its Max conference, Adobe showed early AI features that turn photos into explorable 3D scenes, let users design characters by talking to them, and make photo editing feel like copy and paste.
stories.more: These are "sneaks": Adobe's annual preview of experimental features that haven't shipped as finished products. One experiment turns a flat photo into an explorable 3D scene. Another lets users design AI characters through conversation rather than manual tools, including the ability to "interview" them. A third reworks photo editing into something closer to a copy-and-paste process. Timelines for any of these reaching real products weren't given.

stories.title: DeepL's new Aure model brings tone and pacing to real-time voice translation
stories.summary: DeepL unveiled Aure, a voice model for DeepL Voice that carries a speaker's tone, emotion, emphasis, and speaking pace into real-time translations, aiming to preserve sarcasm and mood shifts across languages.
stories.more: Earlier real-time translation tools have tended to flatten nuance like sarcasm or mood shifts when moving between languages. Aure is designed to carry prosody features, such as intonation, emotional emphasis, and speaking pace, from the original speaker's voice into the translated output. The report doesn't specify which languages or platforms currently support Aure.

stories.title: Google DeepMind mathematically verifies parts of Signal's encryption
stories.summary: Google DeepMind used AI to help mathematically verify key parts of Signal's encryption protocol, a four-week project suggesting AI could make formal verification of software far more practical.
stories.more: Formal verification mathematically proves that code behaves exactly as intended, a process that's traditionally slow and labor-intensive to carry out by hand. DeepMind's project reportedly took about four weeks to check key parts of Signal's encryption using AI. The result is being framed as a hint that AI-assisted formal verification could become practical for checking security-critical software more broadly. The report doesn't specify which exact protocol components were verified or what, if anything, the check turned up.

items.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal

stories.title: Engineer points 48 AI agents at NASA lidar data, finds unmapped Maya pyramid
stories.summary: A Google software engineer reportedly used 48 AI agents to comb through NASA lidar data and identified a previously unmapped Maya pyramid in about 72 hours, according to a widely discussed Hacker News post.
stories.more: The Hacker News submission had gathered 635 points and 247 comments by the time it was fetched. The approach ran 48 AI agents in parallel to sift through lidar scans covering the site. The post doesn't specify which NASA lidar dataset was used or how the finding has been, or will be, verified by archaeologists.

stories.title: Databricks CEO uses an AI agent to surface unfiltered employee feedback
stories.summary: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi uses the company's newly revised Genie agent to learn unvarnished truths from its 12,000 employees, since he can't personally know what's going wrong across the company.
stories.more: Ghodsi acknowledges that at 12,000 employees, he can't personally know everyone, and that staff are unlikely to tell him directly when something is going wrong. Genie, Databricks' AI agent, is positioned to close that gap by surfacing honest feedback he might not otherwise hear. The report doesn't detail how Genie collects or verifies what employees tell it, or what changes, if any, have resulted from its use.

stories.title: Plurai applies self-driving car lessons to make AI agents more reliable
stories.summary: Startup Plurai wants to improve AI agent reliability using methods borrowed from self-driving car development, treating agents as probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.
stories.more: The comparison draws on how end-to-end models for autonomous vehicles are trained and validated before they're trusted on the road. Plurai's premise is that AI agents face a similar challenge: they're probabilistic systems that have to operate reliably once deployed into unpredictable real-world settings. Details on Plurai's specific product, funding, or customers weren't included in the available coverage.

items.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads
items.excerpt: Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.

stories.title: Jensen Huang fell for an alleged Chinese honeypot, report says behavior is common
stories.summary: Wired reports Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by an alleged Chinese sexpionage operation, a well-established espionage tactic. TechCrunch adds that senior industry figures reportedly know such behavior happens and don't act on it.
stories.more: Wired frames China's use of sexpionage as a long-documented intelligence tactic with prior high-profile cases, and questions how the world's most powerful AI executive fell for it anyway. TechCrunch's reporting cites an investment-intelligence consultant who says a lot of senior people in the industry know this kind of thing happens and effectively condone it. Neither report specifies exactly what information or access may have been exposed as a result. It's also unclear from the coverage whether Nvidia or Huang has issued any public response.

stories.title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue tops $10 billion for the first time
stories.summary: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly reached $10 billion, up nearly 50% from $6.7 billion last quarter, driven largely by enterprise sales, though the company still trails Anthropic's revenue and remains cash-flow negative.
stories.more: The jump represents close to 50% growth quarter over quarter, pushed by an enterprise sales push that reportedly includes price cuts aimed at business customers. Despite the revenue growth, OpenAI's adjusted operating losses are said to have climbed to $10.9 billion, meaning the company is still burning more cash than it takes in. By comparison, the reporting describes Anthropic as operating far more efficiently on $17 billion in revenue. Both reports attribute the figures to the companies' financial disclosures without citing a specific filing.

stories.title: DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 to study how DNA affects disease
stories.summary: DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts how DNA sequences and variations affect specific human cell types, aiming to clarify links between genetics and disease.
stories.more: AlphaGenome 2 is a successor model built to read how DNA sequences and their variations play out differently across human cell types. The goal is to give scientists a more detailed view of a problem considered notoriously difficult: tracing how genetic variation contributes to disease. By zooming in at the cellular level, the model is meant to surface clues about disease causes that could eventually point toward new treatments. Specifics on benchmark performance or public availability weren't included in the initial coverage.

stories.title: Anthropic says its AI ported Claude to AMD chips in three days, not months
stories.summary: Anthropic says it used its in-house model Mythos to port Claude to AMD GPUs in just three days with minimal human help, part of a push to reduce reliance on Nvidia's CUDA and cut costs across four chip families.
stories.more: The claim appears in Anthropic's IPO roadshow video, where co-founder Tom Brown described the company's approach to compute, including training and serving Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs. Decoder's reporting frames the AMD port as a task that would normally take months of manual engineering work. No official transcript of the roadshow video was released; one source worked from a transcript extracted independently. The claims rest on Anthropic's own account and haven't been independently verified.

stories.title: AO3 shutdown dispute pits fanfiction readers against authors
stories.summary: A dispute over Archive of Our Own's shutdown has fanfic readers and authors at odds, after one author found her work copied to AO3 mirror sites without her consent.
stories.more: The excerpt centers on one author, whose Heated Rivalry fanfiction was uploaded to AO3 mirror sites without permission, who describes the experience as leaving "a sour taste." Why AO3 itself is shutting down, and who operates the mirror sites, weren't covered in the available excerpt.
